subject: Audit export: sparse sampling, redaction & PSA attachment handling
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@medicosys.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: security-ops@medicosys.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sampling approach and PSA attachments for upcoming SIG delivery

Hi Marcus / Soojin,

Thanks for taking this on. For the SIG/SOC2 evidence bundle request: our audit team needs a clear statement of what you will include from the admin-activity logs and how you plan to sample events for the production snapshot. Two specific asks:

1) If we request a "sparse sample" (e.g., 0.1% uniformly across the 90-day window) can you produce an index mapping (event id -> source shard -> file offset) so we can verify sampling integrity?

2) Do you include PSA/contractual attachments that appear in user activity (signed PDFs, uploaded documents) in the same export, or do you deliver them separately? If separate: preferred delivery options (S3 presigned, Drive folder, or DocuSign/PSA bundle)?

Can you also confirm redaction policy for PII fields in the exported CSV/JSON? We can share a short checklist of reviewers once you propose the format.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Ruiz
Senior Auditor, MedicoSys Compliance

--
Attachment: request_specs.pdf (stub)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@medicosys.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sampling approach and PSA attachments for upcoming SIG delivery

Elena — thanks for the clear asks. High level proposal below; happy to refine.

1) Sparse sampling & index mapping
- We can produce a deterministic sampling manifest: we’ll run a time-seeded hash on event_id and select 1-in-1000 (~0.1%) events across the 90-day window.
- Output format: CSV with columns {event_id, timestamp, model, region, shard, file_name, byte_offset}. This lets you request the exact byte ranges for proofing.
- I’ve attached a short prototype manifest (export_manifest_v1.csv) showing how we map to S3 chunk files.

2) PSA/attachments handling
- Attachments (PSA PDFs, uploaded customer documents) are considered separately from core audit CSVs by default. They can be included in a bundled export, but we recommend separate delivery for chain-of-custody reasons. Options we support:
  a) S3 presigned HTTPS bundle (preferred for large binary sets)
  b) Secure Drive folder (shared link with limited TTL)
  c) DocuSign/PSA: if the PSA is a signed contract that you want as proof, we can include the single PDF in the evidence bundle and add a hash in the manifest.

3) Redaction policy
- By default exports include fully redacted PII fields (email, phone, full IP) unless otherwise required for forensic review. Redactions are logged (redaction_reason column) and we can provide the pre-redaction hashes for verification.

Next steps: confirm (a) sampling ratio acceptable, (b) whether you want attachments combined or delivered separately, and (c) transfer mechanism (S3 or Drive). If you confirm, we’ll schedule an export run and handoff within 3 business days.

Marcus Lin
Sr. Product Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: export_manifest_v1.csv (stub)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sampling approach and PSA attachments for upcoming SIG delivery

Quick operational notes from the infra/ops side — want to make sure expectations are aligned before we run anything.

- Retention windows: core admin-activity ledger (auth events, role changes, admin API calls) are retained 365 days hot, 5 years cold. Audit exports will be taken from the hot store for speed unless you request a historical cold snapshot (longer lead time).

- Export packaging: we produce chunked gzip CSVs (128MB target) with accompanying SHA256 manifest entries. The sample map (attached) demonstrates how we mark chunk boundaries and offsets; you can consume the mapping to rehydrate exact events.

- Redaction specifics:
  * Email addresses — replaced by stable hashed id (sha256) unless you request original; original values will be presented only to approved auditors under NDA and via secure transfer.
  * IP addresses — we keep last-octet redacted by default (x.x.x.0).
  * User display names — redacted when flagged by privacy policy; internal account ids remain for correlation.

- PSA payloads: we will deliver signed PSA PDFs as a separate presigned S3 folder and include the S3 link + SHA256 in the manifest. If you need DocuSign direct delivery, we’ll initiate an envelope and include a DocuSign artifact link in the export manifest.

I attached an example mapping (audit-sample-map.xlsx) and a sample manifest row showing how attachments link to the chunk files.

If you confirm sampling ratio and transfer preference, infra will schedule an export window (we prefer off-peak UTC 01:00–04:00).

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: audit-sample-map.xlsx (stub)

Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 10:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sampling approach and PSA attachments for upcoming SIG delivery

Thanks Marcus / Soojin — this aligns with what we need. A few clarifications before we kick off:

- Sampling ratio: 0.1% (1 in 1000) is acceptable. Please include the deterministic seed in the manifest so we can reproduce the selection.

- Attachments: we prefer separate S3 presigned delivery for the signed PSA bundle. Please include SHA256 for each PDF and the manifest row linking to the chunk. DocuSign link would be a helpful secondary artifact.

- Redaction: acceptable — auditors will request unhashed emails for a short subset under NDA if required; we will provide a signed access request ticket.

Can you confirm estimated delivery timeline (ETA) and whether you need a formal PO/Procurement note from our side to enable S3 cross-account access? We’d like the evidence handoff by next Thursday, 23 Sep 2027.

If you can produce a short delivery checklist (transfer link, manifest, SHA256 list, redaction log, chain-of-custody statement) that would speed our review.

Thanks — I’ll loop in our security operations contact for the access conversation.

Elena
Senior Auditor, MedicoSys
